title: Data and AI
description: Review the data the change produces or uses, its quality and lineage, and the behaviour of any model or AI feature it adds.
expertises: Machine learning and generative AI evaluation
questions: Which data does the change create, transform or rely on, and who owns its definition and quality?
How will the change be measured: which events or metrics, defined where?
If the change uses a model, how is it evaluated before release and monitored after?

sources.title: DAMA International, Data Management Body of Knowledge (DAMA-DMBOK)
Mitchell et al., Model Cards for Model Reporting

specialists.title: Data steward
specialists.focus: Name the owner and definition of each dataset or metric the change touches, and the quality checks it needs: completeness, freshness and validity.
checks: Each metric the change touches has one written definition and an owner.
Freshness, completeness and validity checks run on the affected tables with alert thresholds.

specialists.title: Analytics engineer
specialists.focus: Check the events, schemas and transformations that measure the change, and that existing dashboards and reports keep working.
checks: New events follow the tracking plan naming and carry a schema version.
Dashboards and models that read changed fields are listed and tested before release.

specialists.title: ML and AI evaluator
specialists.focus: For a model or AI feature, define the evaluation set, the quality and safety metrics and the threshold that blocks release.
checks: The evaluation set is separate from training data and represents the users the model serves.
The release threshold for quality and safety metrics is set before results are seen.

specialists.title: AI risk lead
specialists.focus: Document the model's intended use, limits and failure modes, the human oversight in place and the obligations that apply to the use case.
checks: Intended use, known limits and prohibited uses are written in a model or system card.
The use case is classified against the AI Act risk categories with legal.

evidence: Data contracts, schemas or dbt models for the datasets involved, with their owner.
Tracking plan or metric definitions for the change.
Evaluation dataset, results and thresholds for any model or prompt change, with the date of the run.
Model card or AI use-case record with intended use, limits and oversight.
challenge: Which downstream report, model or customer export breaks if this field changes meaning or format?
Would we notice a silent drop in data quality, and how fast?
On which inputs does the model fail, and what does the user see then?
Does the evaluation represent production data, or only the examples we expected?
decision_criteria: Proceed when owned data definitions, quality checks and lineage cover what the change touches.
Revise when no metric or event can show whether the change worked.
Block an AI feature without an evaluation run against agreed thresholds or without a documented human fallback.
Escalate to the legal owner a use case that may fall under a regulated AI category.
